head.i: Negotiatorem clericum tanquam pestem fugiendum. Hier.

main_text.p: Dist. 88, C. Negotiatorem.) Negotiatorem clericum, & ex inope diuite, & ex ignobili glo-riosum quasi quandam pestem fuge.
Dist. 46. C. Non licet) Non licet fœnerari ministris altaris, vel in sacerdotali ordine constitutis, vel usuras vel lucra quæ sexcupla dicuntur, accipere.
Dist. 47. C. Episcopus.) Ex Canonibus Apostolorum. Episcopus aut presbyter aut diaconus, usuras à debitoribus exigens, aut definat, aut certè deponatur.

Et mox. C. Quoniam multi.) Ex Concilio Niceno. Quoniam multi sub regula constituti avaritiam & turpia lucra sectantur, oblitiqué diuinæ scripturæ dicentis: Qui pecuniam suam non dederit ad usuram, &c. mutuum dantes centesimas usuras exigunt, iustè censuit magna & sancta Synodus, ut si quis inuentus fuerit post hanc deffinitionem usuras accipiens, aut aliquam adinuentionem faciens, vel quolibet modo negotia transfigens, aut hemiolia, id est, sexcupla exigens, vel aliquid tale prorsus excogitans, turpis lucri gratia, deijciatur à clero, & alienus existat à regula.
Item paulò post ex Concilio Elibertino, Si quis

page.notes: Faint page number at the top left, uncertain. Running head ends in a mark read as a hyphen or ornament, marked [?]. "Quoniam multi" is underlined in the print and is rendered in italics. Reading "sexcupla" for the printed "fexcupla" and "usuras" for "vfuras" follows the long-s and u/v rules. Some words in the mid-page paragraph are slightly blurred and may need checking, notably "oblitiqué" and "deffinitionem" (kept as printed).
